english.heading: Plant Selection and Guilds
body: Choose plants that work together—and change the planting as it grows.

heading.text: Kgetho ya dimela le dihlopha tsa dimela (guilds)
heading.backTranslation: Selection of plants and plant groups (guilds)

body.text: Kgetha dimela tse sebetsang mmoho—mme o fetole temo ha e ntse e hola.
body.backTranslation: Choose plants that work together—and change the farming/garden as it grows.

english.heading: Plant Selection and Guilds
body: A fruit tree needs light, water, soil nutrients and room. Support plants can supply food, leafy mulch, flowers and living cover.  Give each plant a useful job. Keep observing whether it helps the tree and the household. Which jobs does your planting need?

heading.text: Kgetho ya dimela le dihlopha tsa dimela (guilds)
heading.backTranslation: Selection of plants and plant groups (guilds)

body.text: Sefate sa ditholwana se hloka lesedi, metsi, nutrients tsa mobu le sebaka. Support plants di ka fana ka dijo, mulch ya mahlaku, dipalesa le sekwahelo se phelang. Fa semela ka seng mosebetsi o molemo. Tswela pele o hlokomela hore na se thusa sefate le lelapa. Ke mesebetsi efe e hlokehang temong ya hao?
body.backTranslation: A fruit tree needs light, water, soil nutrients and space. Support plants can provide food, leaf mulch, flowers and a living cover. Give each plant a good job. Keep watching whether it helps the tree and the household. What functions are needed in your garden/field?

english.heading: Start With the Site
body: Find out what is limiting growth before choosing a plant.

body.text: Fumana hore na ke eng e thibelang kgolo pele o kgetha semela.
body.backTranslation: Find out what is blocking growth before you choose a plant.

english.heading: Start With the Site
body: Check sunlight, drainage, soil condition and water availability. Nitrogen is only one possible limitation.  Compare the soil beneath mulch with exposed soil. Choose support plants that fit the actual conditions. What does this site need first?

body.text: Hlahloba lesedi la letsatsi, ho tswa ha metsi mobung, boemo ba mobu le ho fumaneha ha metsi. Nitrogen ke e nngwe feela ya dintho tse ka nnang tsa thibela kgolo. Bapisa mobu o ka tlasa mulch le mobu o pepeneneng. Kgetha support plants tse loketseng maemo a sebele. Sebaka sena se hloka eng pele?
body.backTranslation: Check sunlight, water draining/coming out in the soil, soil condition and availability of water. Nitrogen is only one of the things that can possibly hinder growth. Compare soil under mulch with bare/exposed soil. Choose support plants suited to the actual conditions. What does this place need first?

english.heading: Give Every Plant a Job
body: A useful guild produces benefits you can observe.

heading.text: Fana ka mosebetsi ho semela ka seng

body.text: Guild e molemo e hlahisa melemo eo o ka e bonang.
body.backTranslation: A good guild produces benefits that you can see.

english.heading: Give Every Plant a Job
body: Choose members for food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or ground cover. One plant may do several jobs.  By the end, plan a guild, explain how residues feed soil, and decide which support plants to keep, cut or remove. Which job is still missing?

heading.text: Fana ka mosebetsi ho semela ka seng

body.text: Kgetha ditho tsa guild bakeng sa dijo, nitrogen fixation, mulch, dipalesa kapa sekwahelo sa mobu. Semela se le seng se ka etsa mesebetsi e mengata. Qetellong, rera guild, hlalosa kamoo masalla a fepang mobu kateng, mme o etse qeto ya hore na ke support plants dife tseo o tla di boloka, ho di seha kapa ho di tlosa. Ke mosebetsi ofe o ntseng o haella?
body.backTranslation: Choose the members of the guild for food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or ground cover. One plant can do many functions. Finally, plan the guild, explain how the leftovers/residues feed the soil, and decide which support plants you will keep, cut back or remove. Which function is still lacking?

english.heading: Look for Root Nodules
body: Legumes work with rhizobia in nodules on their roots.

heading.backTranslation: Look for nodules on the roots

body.text: Legumes di sebetsa mmoho le rhizobia ka nodules tse metsong ya tsona.
body.backTranslation: Legumes work together with rhizobia through nodules that are on their roots.

english.heading: Look for Root Nodules
body: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.  Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions. Can you find the nodules?

heading.backTranslation: Look for nodules on the roots

body.text: Dibaktheria (bacteria) tsena di fetola nitrogen e tswang moyeng hore e be mefuta eo legume e ka e sebedisang. Batla nodules ho semela sa legume seo o sa se hlokeng. Nodulation le kgolo di itshetlehile ka semela, dibaktheria (bacteria) tse loketseng le maemo a kgolo. Na o ka fumana nodules?
body.backTranslation: These bacteria (bacteria) change nitrogen from the air into forms that the legume can use. Look for nodules on the legume plant you need. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria (bacteria) and growing conditions. Can you find nodules?

english.heading: Return Leaves to the Soil
body: Nitrogen in plant material becomes useful as that material breaks down.

body.text: Nitrogen e ka hara dikarolo tsa semela e ba molemo ha dikarolo tseo di bola.
body.backTranslation: Nitrogen that is inside the parts of the plant becomes good/useful when those parts rot.

english.heading: Return Leaves to the Soil
body: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.  This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree. Which residues can you return?

body.text: Busetsa makala a nang le mahlaku a loketseng a faotsweng, mahlaku a wileng le masalla a dijalo e le mulch. Diphedi tsa mobu di lokolla nutrients nakong ya decomposition. Sena se nka nako. Legume e phelang ha se phaephe ya manyolo e yang sefateng sa ditholwana hang-hang. Ke masalla afe ao o ka a busetsang?
body.backTranslation: Return branches with suitable leaves that were pruned, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition. This takes time. A living legume is not a fertiliser pipe going to the fruit tree immediately. Which residues can you return?

english.heading: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
body: Sesbania sesban can supply fast growth and leafy mulch.

heading.text: Sesbania e na le mosebetsi o molemo

body.text: Sesbania sesban e ka fana ka kgolo e potlakileng le mulch ya mahlaku.
body.backTranslation: Sesbania sesban can provide fast growth and leaf mulch.

english.heading: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
body: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.  Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases. Where could you manage its growth?

heading.text: Sesbania e na le mosebetsi o molemo

body.text: Ke semela se indigenous ho KwaZulu-Natal. Maemong a futhumetseng a loketseng, laola sehlahla sena se sa phelang nako e telele kapa sefate se senyane e le support plant. Dumella sebaka bakeng sa kgolo ya sona. Faola bakeng sa mulch, mme o se hlahlobe hape ha moriti kapa tlhodisano ya metsi e eketseha. O ka laola kgolo ya sona kae?
body.backTranslation: It is a plant indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this long-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant. Allow space for its growth. Prune it for mulch, and check it again when shade or water competition increases. Where can you manage its growth?

english.heading: Check the Full Plant Name
body: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different species.

heading.text: Hlahloba lebitso le felletseng la semela
heading.backTranslation: Check the full name of the plant

body.text: Sesbania sesban le Sesbania punicea ke mefuta e fapaneng.
body.backTranslation: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different species.

english.heading: Check the Full Plant Name
body: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.  Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier verify the species?

heading.text: Hlahloba lebitso le felletseng la semela
heading.backTranslation: Check the full name of the plant

body.text: Sesbania punicea ke red sesbania e invasive. Dikoko tsa yona tsa dipeo (pods) di na le mapheo a mane a tsamayang ka bolelele. Netefatsa hore ke sefe ka botanical guidance e tshepehang. Hlahloba lebitso le feletseng pele o jala. Hlompha project species list e dumellanweng, ho kenyeletswa thibelo efe kapa efe mabapi le Sesbania sesban. Na morekisi a ka netefatsa mofuta?
body.backTranslation: Sesbania punicea is an invasive red sesbania. Its seed pods (pods) have four wings running lengthwise. Confirm which one it is using reliable botanical guidance. Check the full name before you plant. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction concerning Sesbania sesban. Can the seller confirm the species?

english.heading: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
body: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can provide peas, leafy material and nitrogen fixation.

heading.text: Pigeon pea e fana le ka dijo

body.text: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—e ka fana ka dierekisi, thepa ya mahlaku le nitrogen fixation.
body.backTranslation: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can provide peas, leaf material and nitrogen fixation.

english.heading: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
body: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.  Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest. Are you growing this plant for peas or mulch?

heading.text: Pigeon pea e fana le ka dijo

body.text: Sebedisa sebaka se nang le letsatsi, se tswang metsi hantle. Ke support shrub e sa phelang nako e telele; serame le metsi a emeng di ka e fokotsa. Etsa qeto ya hore na semela se seng le se seng se fana haholo ka dierekisi kapa ka thepa e nang le mahlaku. Ho seha ka makgetlo a mangata ka matla ho ka se senya le ho fokotsa thobo ya dijo. Na o hodisa semela sena bakeng sa dierekisi kapa mulch?
body.backTranslation: Use a sunny, well-drained place. It is a long-lived support shrub; frost and standing water can reduce it. Decide whether each plant gives mostly peas or leafy material. Heavy, frequent cutting can damage it and reduce food yield. Are you growing this plant for peas or mulch?

english.heading: Choose for Place and Size
body: A useful support tree in one place may be too large or unsuitable in another.

heading.text: Kgetha ho latela sebaka le boholo
heading.backTranslation: Choose according to place and size

body.text: Support tree e sebetsang sebakeng se seng e ka ba kgolo ho feta tekano kapa e sa loketse sebakeng se seng.
body.backTranslation: A support tree that works in one place can be bigger than appropriate or unsuitable in another place.

english.heading: Choose for Place and Size
body: Compare mature crown, roots, shade, rainfall and temperature. Check locally appropriate species and planting rules.  Put large support trees where they have space. For a small young guild, a manageable shrub may be easier to maintain. How large will this plant become?

heading.text: Kgetha ho latela sebaka le boholo
heading.backTranslation: Choose according to place and size

body.text: Bapisa crown e hodileng ka botlalo, metso, moriti, pula le motjheso. Hlahloba mefuta e loketseng sebaka le melao ya ho jala. Beha support trees tse kgolo moo di nang le sebaka. Bakeng sa guild e nyenyane e ntjha, sehlahlana se laolehang se ka ba bonolo ho hlokomela ho feta. Semela sena se tla ba seholo hakae?
body.backTranslation: Compare the fully grown crown, roots, shade, rain and heat. Check the species suited to the area and the planting rules. Place large support trees where they have space. For a small new guild, a manageable shrub may be easier to look after. How big will this plant become?

english.heading: Annual Cover Has a Place
body: Sunn hemp can cover a suitable warm-season gap before the next crop.

heading.text: Annual cover e na le sebaka sa yona

body.text: Sunn hemp e ka kwahela sekgeo se loketseng nakong e futhumetseng pele ho sejalo se latelang.
body.backTranslation: Sunn hemp can cover a suitable gap in the warm season before the next crop.

english.heading: Annual Cover Has a Place
body: Grow it where its season and space fit the plan. Its contribution depends on growth, nodulation and the material returned.  After cutting, allow for decomposition. An annual cover crop plays a different role from a longer-lived support shrub. When will this space be needed again?

heading.text: Annual cover e na le sebaka sa yona

body.text: E hodise moo sehla sa yona le sebaka di lekanang le morero. Seabo sa yona se itshetlehile ka kgolo, nodulation le thepa e busetswang. Ka mora ho e seha, dumella nako ya decomposition. Annual cover crop e bapala karolo e fapaneng le support shrub e phelang nako e telele ho feta. Sebaka sena se tla hlokahala neng hape?
body.backTranslation: Grow it where its season and space match the purpose. Its contribution depends on growth, nodulation and the material returned. After cutting it, allow time for decomposition. An annual cover crop plays a different role from a longer-lived support shrub. When will this space be needed again?

english.heading: Leave Room Around the Tree
body: Keep the young fruit tree in light and retain access for care.

body.text: Boloka sefate sa ditholwana se sa le senyane se na le lesedi, mme o boloke tsela ya ho fihlella bakeng sa tlhokomelo.
body.backTranslation: Keep the young fruit tree in light, and keep an access path for care.

english.heading: Leave Room Around the Tree
body: Keep an open establishment basin and access to the fruit tree. Place temporary support plants where their size and water use can be managed.  Put leafy cuttings where mulch is needed. Neighbouring fruit trees can share support strips between them. Can you reach both plants as they grow?

body.text: Boloka establishment basin e bulehileng le tsela ya ho fihlella sefate sa ditholwana. Beha support plants tsa nakwana moo boholo le tshebediso ya tsona ya metsi di ka laolwang. Beha makala a nang le mahlaku a sehilweng moo mulch e hlokahalang. Difate tse haufi tsa ditholwana di ka arolelana support strips tse pakeng tsa tsona. Na o ka kgona ho fihlella dimela tsena ka bobedi ha di ntse di hola?
body.backTranslation: Keep the establishment basin and access to the fruit tree open. Place temporary support plants where their size and water use can be managed. Put branches with pruned leaves where mulch is needed. Nearby fruit trees can share support strips between them. Can you reach both these plants while they grow?

english.heading: Build a Layered Support Guild
body: Combine seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary small trees.

body.text: Kopanya dimela tse kwahelang mobu nakong ya sehla, support shrubs le difate tse nyenyane tsa nakwana.
body.backTranslation: Combine seasonal ground-cover plants, support shrubs and small temporary trees.

english.heading: Build a Layered Support Guild
body: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.  Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access. Which layers fit your site?

body.text: Cowpea e kwahela dibaka tse bulehileng tse nang le letsatsi. Pigeon pea e fana ka dijo le thepa e nang le mahlaku. Sesbania sesban e laolwang e ka fana ka support plant e telele ho feta, ya nakwana. Eketsa dimela tse loketseng, tse nang le dipalesa le tsa mulch. Boloka kutu ya sefate sa mango (trunk) e hlakile, mme o laole lesedi, metsi le tsela ya ho fihlella. Ke mekgahlelo efe e loketseng sebaka sa hao?
body.backTranslation: Cowpea covers open sunny spaces. Pigeon pea gives food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can give a taller, temporary support plant. Add suitable plants, flowering ones and mulch ones. Keep the mango tree trunk (trunk) clear, and manage light, water and access. Which layers suit your space?

english.heading: How Many Support Plants?
body: Plan abundant support where the site and your care can sustain it.

body.text: Rera support plants tse ngata moo sebaka le tlhokomelo ya hao di ka di tswelletsang pele.
body.backTranslation: Plan many support plants where your space and care can keep them going.

english.heading: How Many Support Plants?
body: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.  There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin. How much support can you maintain?

body.text: Bala support plants tse nang le lehong ho pholletsa le dibaka tse pakeng tsa difate tsa ditholwana. Jala dimela tse loketseng tse kwahelang mobu ho ya ka sebaka. Ha ho na palo e tshwanang e sebetsang bakeng sa sefate se seng le se seng sa ditholwana. Fetola palo ya dimela ho ya ka metsi, mobu, boholo ba semela le bokgoni ba hao ba ho faola le ho fokotsa (thinning). O ka hlokomela support plants tse kae?
body.backTranslation: Count the woody support plants across the spaces between the fruit trees. Plant suitable ground-cover plants according to the space. There is no single number that works for every fruit tree. Change the number of plants according to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin (thinning). How many support plants can you look after?

english.heading: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
body: Watch the branch fall onto the cut leaves.

heading.text: Chop-and-drop bakeng sa lesedi le mulch

body.text: Shebella ha lekala le wela hodima mahlaku a sehilweng.
body.backTranslation: Watch as the branch falls on top of the cut leaves.

english.heading: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
body: Prune a support tree and return suitable leafy cuttings to the soil. The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.  Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas. Which plant needs a cut—and how much?

heading.text: Chop-and-drop bakeng sa lesedi le mulch

body.text: Faola support tree mme o kgutlisetse mobung makala a nang le mahlaku a loketseng a sehilweng. Video e bontsha lekala le sehilweng: support tree e ntse e eme. Tlohela mahlaku a lekaneng a phetseng hantle hore semela se fole. Lekanyetsa ho seha ho ya ka mofuta wa semela. Qoba ho seha ka matla ka makgetlo a mangata ho pigeon pea, haholo-holo ha o e jala bakeng sa dierekisi. Ke semela sefe se hlokang ho sehwa, mme ka bokae?
body.backTranslation: Prune the support tree and return suitable leafy cut branches to the soil. The video shows a cut branch: the support tree is still standing. Leave enough healthy leaves so that the plant can recover. Adjust the cutting according to the kind of plant. Avoid cutting hard and often on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it for peas. Which plant needs cutting, and how much?

english.heading: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
body: Spread suitable cut material over the soil, with the trunk and root collar clear.

heading.text: Boloka mulch hole le kutu ya sefate (trunk)
heading.backTranslation: Keep mulch away from the tree trunk

body.text: Hasa thepa e loketseng e sehilweng hodima mobu, kutu ya sefate (trunk) le root collar di sa kwahelwe.
body.backTranslation: Spread suitable cut material over the soil, with the tree trunk (trunk) and root collar left uncovered.

english.heading: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
body: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.  Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition. Is the root collar still clear?

heading.text: Boloka mulch hole le kutu ya sefate (trunk)
heading.backTranslation: Keep mulch away from the tree trunk

body.text: Mulch e sireletsa bokahodimo ba mobu, e thusa ho boloka mongobo, mme e busetsa thepa ya organic. Boloka tsela ya ho fihlella bakeng sa ho nosetsa le ho hlahloba. Seha thepa dikotwana tse laolehang, mme o tswelepele ho shebisisa mongobo le decomposition. Na root collar e ntse e sa kwahelwe?
body.backTranslation: Mulch protects the soil surface, helps keep moisture, and returns organic material. Keep access for watering and checking. Cut the material in manageable pieces, and keep watching moisture and decomposition. Is the root collar still uncovered?

english.heading: Choose the Right Comfrey
body: Bocking 14 comfrey can supply cut leaves for mulch.

body.text: Bocking 14 comfrey e ka fana ka mahlaku a sehilweng bakeng sa mulch.
body.backTranslation: Bocking 14 comfrey can provide cut leaves for mulch.

english.heading: Choose the Right Comfrey
body: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.  Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree. Is this a good permanent place for the clump?

body.text: Fumana cultivar e nepahetseng. Bocking 14 ha e phatlalale ka viable seed, empa dikotwana tsa metso di ka mela hape. E bee moo e nang le sebaka le mongobo o lekaneng. Seha mahlaku ha e ntse e fola; o se ke wa pitlaganya sefate se senyane sa ditholwana. Na sena ke sebaka se setle sa ka ho sa feleng sa sehlopha sena sa comfrey?
body.backTranslation: Find a suitable cultivar. Bocking 14 ha is propagated by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again. Put it where there is enough space and enough moisture. Cut the leaves while it is still recovering; do not crowd/trample a small fruit tree. Is this a good permanent place for this group of comfrey?

english.heading: Observe Helpful Insects
body: Flowers can provide resources for useful insects.

body.text: Dipalesa di ka fana ka mehlodi bakeng sa dikokwanyana (insects) tse thusang.
body.backTranslation: Flowers can give resources [?] for helpful insects.

english.heading: Observe Helpful Insects
body: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.  Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control. What is the insect actually doing?

body.text: Ladybirds tse ngata di ja aphids; parasitoid wasps tse ding di hlasela dikokwanyana tse senyang dijalo (pests). Ditho tse nang le dipalesa tse kang African basil di ka eketsa mehlodi. Shebisisa hore ke dikokwanyana (insects) dife tse etelang le hore na tshenyo e a fetoha. Semela se nang le dipalesa ha se tiise ho laolwa ha dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests). Kokwanyana eo ka nnete e etsa eng?
body.backTranslation: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack insects that damage crops (pests). Flowering members such as African basil can add resources. Check which insects (insects) visit and whether the damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee control of damaging insects (pests). What does that insect actually do?

english.heading: Give Flowers Their Space
body: Wild garlic can be a flowering member where the site suits it.

body.text: Wild garlic e ka ba setho se nang le dipalesa moo sebaka se e loketseng.
body.backTranslation: Wild garlic can be a member that has flowers where the place suits it.

english.heading: Give Flowers Their Space
body: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.  Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak. Where can flowers grow without crowding?

body.text: Tulbaghia violacea e na le mahlaku a masesane le dipalesa tse mmala wa lilac. Bea sehlopha sa yona moo se nang le lesedi le sebaka sa ho hola. Shebisisa dikokwanyana (insects) tse etelang. O se ke wa tshepisa hore sedikadikwe (ring) sa wild garlic se tla leleka dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests) kapa hore se tla fedisa ho phatlalala ho kgolo ha tsona. Dipalesa di ka mela kae ntle le ho pitlagana?
body.backTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac-coloured flowers. Place its group where there is light and room to grow. Watch the insects (insects) that visit. Do not promise that a ring (ring) of wild garlic will drive away pests (pests) or that it will stop their spread or growth. Where can the flowers grow without crowding?

english.heading: Bring the Jobs Together
body: Choose useful partners while protecting the mango's growing space.

body.text: Kgetha balekane ba thusang ha o ntse o sireletsa sebaka sa ho hola sa mango.
body.backTranslation: Choose partners that help while protecting the mango's growing space.

english.heading: Bring the Jobs Together
body: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.  Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow. Does each member have space and a job?

body.text: Kopanya support functions tseo sebaka sa hao se di hlokang: nitrogen fixation, dijo, mulch, dipalesa le dimela tse kwahelang mobu. Dimela tse ding di sebetsa mesebetsi e mengata. Boloka sebaka sa kutu ya sefate (trunk) le tsela di bulehile. Hlahloba hape setho se seng le se seng ha mango le dimela tse haufi le yona di ntse di hola. Na setho ka seng se na le sebaka hammoho le mosebetsi?
body.backTranslation: Combine the support functions that your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground-cover plants. Some plants perform many functions. Keep the trunk (trunk) area and the path open. Check again each member, the mango and the plants near it, as they grow. Does each member have both space and a function?

english.heading: Food Cover Also Competes
body: Sweet potato can cover ground and provide food in a suitable sunny space.

heading.text: Sekwahelo sa dijo le sona se a tlhodisana
heading.backTranslation: A food cover/ground cover also competes

body.text: Sweet potato e ka kwahela mobu le ho fana ka dijo sebakeng se loketseng se nang le letsatsi.
body.backTranslation: Sweet potato can cover the soil and provide food in a suitable sunny area.

english.heading: Food Cover Also Competes
body: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.  Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Is this cover helping the tree establish?

heading.text: Sekwahelo sa dijo le sona se a tlhodisana
heading.backTranslation: A food cover/ground cover also competes

body.text: Boloka makala a yona a hasanang (vines) hole le sefate se senyane sa ditholwana, mme o boloke tsela ya tlhokomelo. Metso ya yona le yona e sebedisa metsi le nutrients. Moo mehlodi e sa lekaneng, bapisa se kwahelang mobu se phelang le mulch basin e tlwaelehileng. Na sekwahelo sena se thusa sefate ho thehwa hantle (establishment)?
body.backTranslation: Keep its spreading branches (vines) away from the young fruit tree, and keep an access path for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients. Where resources are not enough, compare a living ground cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Does this cover help the tree to establish well (establishment)?

english.heading: First, Establish the Guild
body: Start while the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.

body.text: Qala ha sefate sa ditholwana se senyane le support plants tsa sona di na le lesedi le metsi a lekaneng.
body.backTranslation: Start when the small fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.

english.heading: First, Establish the Guild
body: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.  Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for every plant through establishment?

body.text: Jala sehleng se loketseng, beha mulch, mme o tswelepele ho nosetsa nakong ya ho thehwa ha semela. Boloka sekgeo sa ho fihlella se bulehile. Qala ka palo ya support plants eo o ka e hlokomelang. Shebisisa ho phela le kgolo pele o eketsa tse ding. Na o ka kgona ho hlokomela semela se seng le se seng ho fihlela se thehilwe hantle?
body.backTranslation: Plant in a suitable season, put on mulch, and keep watering during plant establishment. Keep the access gap open. Start with the number of support plants that you can look after. Watch survival and growth before adding more. Can you look after each plant until it is well established?

english.heading: Thin as the Fruit Tree Grows
body: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce selected support plants. Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.  Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition. Which support plants should now give way?

heading.text: Thinning ha sefate sa ditholwana se hola
heading.backTranslation: Thinning as the fruit tree grows

body.text: Ha ho faola ho se ho sa lekana, fokotsa support plants tse kgethilweng. Seha fatshe support plants tse kgethilweng tse tlhodisanang ho bula sebaka. Thepa e sehilweng e loketseng e ka sala e le mulch: sena ke ho fokotsa (thinning) ka chop-and-drop. Laola ho mela hape ho boloka sebaka se butsweng. Hlahloba lesedi, mongobo wa mobu le kgolo; ho fokotsa (thinning) ha ho emise hang-hang tlhodisano ya metso. Ke support plants dife tse lokelang ho tlohela sebaka jwale?
body.backTranslation: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce the chosen support plants. Cut down the competing chosen support plants to open up space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning (thinning) by chop-and-drop. Manage regrowth to keep the opened space. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning (thinning) does not immediately stop root competition. Which support plants should give up space now?

english.heading: Move Support Into the Light
body: As shade increases, renew sun-loving support plants in open edges and younger plantings.

heading.backTranslation: Take support plants to the light

body.text: Ha moriti o eketseha, ntjhafatsa support plants tse ratang letsatsi mahlakoreng a bulehileng le dijalong tse ntjha.
body.backTranslation: As shade increases, renew the sun-loving support plants on the open sides and in new plantings.

english.heading: Move Support Into the Light
body: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.  Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next useful sunny space?

heading.backTranslation: Take support plants to the light

body.text: Busetsa makala a faotsweng a nang le molemo ho difate tse seng di thehilwe hantle. Boloka dimela tse haufi feela moo di ntseng di sebetsa hantle. Difate tse hodileng tsa ditholwana di ntse di hloka nutrients. Shebisisa kgolo, thobo le maemo a mobu; support plants ha di tlose tlhoko eo. Sebaka se latelang se nang le letsatsi se thusang ke kae?
body.backTranslation: Return useful pruned branches to trees that are already well established. Keep nearby plants only where they are still working well. Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Watch growth, yield and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next sunny place that helps?

english.heading: Let Observation Decide
body: Keep a short record of how the guild performs.

heading.text: Etsa qeto ka seo o se bonang
heading.backTranslation: Make a decision about what you see

body.text: Boloka rekoto e kgutshwane ya kamoo guild e sebetsang kateng.
body.backTranslation: Keep a short record of how the guild is working.

english.heading: Let Observation Decide
body: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.  Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here. What evidence would make you change the guild?

heading.text: Etsa qeto ka seo o se bonang
heading.backTranslation: Make a decision about what you see

body.text: Hlahloba kgolo ya sefate sa ditholwana, moriti, mongobo wa mobu, thobo e nang le molemo le tshenyo ya dikokwanyana tse senyang (pests). Ngola seo se sehilweng, se kgutlisitsweng kapa se tlositsweng. Sebedisa dintho tsena tseo o di shebisisitseng ho fetola moralo le tlhokomelo. Semela se tshwanelwa ke sebaka sa sona ka lebaka la seo se se etsang mona. Ke bopaki bofe bo ka o etsang hore o fetole guild?
body.backTranslation: Check the fruit tree's growth, shade, soil moisture, useful yield and damage from damaging insects (pests). Write down what was cut, returned or removed. Use these things you have observed to change the design and care. A plant deserves its place because of what it does here. What evidence could make you change the guild?

english.heading: Plan One Real Guild
body: Choose one fruit tree and mark a layout you can manage.

heading.text: Rala guild e le nngwe ya sebele

body.text: Kgetha sefate se le seng sa ditholwana mme o tshwaye moralo oo o ka kgonang ho o laola.
body.backTranslation: Choose one fruit tree and mark the design that you can manage.

english.heading: Plan One Real Guild
body: Record the tree, site conditions and missing jobs. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave access.  Write down what will trigger pruning or thinning. Agree the species list with the project team where required. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?

heading.text: Rala guild e le nngwe ya sebele

body.text: Ngola sefate, maemo a sebaka le mesebetsi e haellang. Reha support species ka botlalo, o tshwaye palo ya ho qala mme o siye tsela ya ho fihlella. Ngola seo se tla susumetsa ho faola kapa thinning. Dumellana ka lenane la mefuta le sehlopha sa porojeke moo ho hlokahalang. Na ho na le motho e mong ya ka kgonang ho o hlalosetsa leano la hao hape?
body.backTranslation: Record the tree, site conditions and missing functions. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave an access path. Record what will prompt pruning or thinning. Agree a species list with the project team where needed. Is there anyone else who can explain your plan again?

english.heading: Plant, Observe, Adjust
body: Start one suitable guild and care for it through its first stage.

body.text: Qala guild e le nngwe e loketseng mme o e hlokomele mohatong wa yona wa pele.
body.backTranslation: Start one suitable guild and look after it in its first stage.

english.heading: Plant, Observe, Adjust
body: Use the right species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return useful biomass and protect the fruit tree.  Review the planting as crowns expand. Keep, cut, replace or remove each support plant when its role changes. What will you do first—and when will you review it?

body.text: Sebedisa mefuta e nepahetseng, palo ya dimela e ka laolwang le sebaka sa ho hola. Kgutlisetsa biomass e thusang mme o sireletse sefate sa ditholwana. Hlahloba jalo hape ha crowns di ntse di hola. Boloka, seha, ntjhafatsa kapa tlosa support plant ka nngwe ha mosebetsi wa yona o fetoha. O tla etsa eng pele, mme o tla e hlahloba neng?
body.backTranslation: Use suitable species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return helpful biomass and protect the fruit tree. Check the planting again as the crowns grow. Keep, cut back, renew or remove each support plant when its function changes. What will you do first, and when will you check it?
